name: UAF anti-money-laundering kit for property brokers, notaries and small real-estate firms
buyer: Property brokers, small inmobiliarias and notaries registered with the UAF
trigger: Ley 19.913 and UAF Circular 62 (Mar 2025): compliance officer, ROS via the UAF Portal de Entidades Reportantes, analysis log, beneficial-owner identification, staff training, registration update within 10 business days. Brokers, notaries and inmobiliarias accounted for 55% of UAF fines in 2018 (Diario Estrategia). A broker licensing bill (Boletin 18.241-03, May 2026 Senate bill) would add more duties.
evidence: Circular 62: https://guerrero.cl/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DOC_Circular-N°62-UAF.pdf ; DLA Piper: https://www.dlapiper.com/es-ar/insights/publications/2025/03/chile-financial-analysis-unit ; DF on sanctions: https://www.df.cl/empresas/banca-instituciones-financieras/uaf-inicio-80-procesos-sancionatorios-por-incumplir-normas-anti-lavado ; bill: https://www.diarioconstitucional.cl/2026/05/19/iniciativa-legal-busca-regular-el-corretaje-de-propiedades-y-exige-licencia-para-ejercer-la-actividad/
existing: Competitor search 'software cumplimiento UAF corredores de propiedades inmobiliarias oficial de cumplimiento ROS Chile plataforma' found no broker-specific Chilean platform; only Simplo explainers. The UAF portal itself is free but does not log analysis or KYC.
unchecked: Number of registered brokers; whether broker CRMs (e.g. portal-linked) bundle UAF modules; AML compliance vendors serving larger firms; the two broker bills' status; willingness to pay by small brokers; a possible overlap with larger vendors for notaries.

first_check.duty: Ley 19.913 art. 3 and UAF Circular 62 (issued 18/19 March 2025, in force 1 June 2025) apply to corredores de propiedades, empresas de gestión inmobiliaria and notarios. Duties: UAF registration from the start of activity, with changes reported within 10 business days; a compliance officer; a prevention manual updated every 2 years; annual staff training; periodic screening against UN Security Council lists; beneficial-owner identification; ROS reports; records kept 5 years. Breaches are punished with admonitions or fines under Ley 19.913. I did not confirm exact UF ranges in this session.
first_check.market: A DIPRES document gives the UAF register at 31 March 2015: 5,640 reporting entities in total, including 1,037 corredores de propiedades and 478 empresas de gestión inmobiliaria. Notaries number a few hundred, but I did not find the figure. I found no current (2025/26) count. The UAF publishes its register every six months on uaf.cl. Broker bill Boletín 18.241-03 is in the Senate; I did not verify its status.
first_check.competitor: Gesintel AMLupdate (gesintel.cl) offers due diligence, monitoring, a beneficial-owner finder (UBOfinder) and onboarding. It explicitly targets Notarios, Grandes Empresas and other sectors, so it is a real competitor for notaries. It does not list brokers, inmobiliarias or SMEs, and shows no public pricing. My searches found no Chilean compliance tool specific to brokers or SMEs. Law-firm consultancies (manuals, outsourced compliance officer) are the probable substitute, but I did not check them. The free UAF portal only takes reports. I did not check whether broker CRMs bundle a UAF module (not_reached).
first_check.reason: The duty is real and in force. Ley 19.913 art. 3 and UAF Circular 62 (issued March 2025, in force since 1 June 2025) apply to property brokers, real-estate management firms and notaries. They must keep UAF registration, appoint a compliance officer, keep a prevention manual updated every two years, train staff every year, screen clients against UN lists, identify beneficial owners and file ROS reports. The UAF fines these sectors heavily: real-estate firms were among the most sanctioned in 2021, mostly for a missing manual or missing training. Gesintel's AMLupdate is aimed at notaries and large firms, not small brokers. I found no broker-specific SME tool. The market is small: about 1,037 brokers and 478 inmobiliarias in 2015. Small brokers file few ROS, so they may pay little. An MVP (manual, training, list-screening log) is simple.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The real limits are a small market of a few thousand UAF-registered entities across all sectors, weak enforcement among unlicensed brokers, and Circular 62 letting micro/small firms name the owner as compliance officer. Gesintel competes only for notaries. Unverified: law-firm outsourced-compliance services and broker CRMs (not_reached).
challenge_check.reason: Nothing I found kills this idea. My Spanish searches turned up no AML tool built for Chilean brokers or SMEs, and no broker CRM with a UAF module. The UAF portal only receives reports. Gesintel lists notaries but not brokers, inmobiliarias or SMEs, and shows no pricing. Three things hold it back. The market is small: about 3,500 to 8,000 reporting entities across all sectors, with no broker-specific count found. Brokers do not need a licence, so many unregistered ones probably ignore the duty. And Circular 62 lets micro and small firms name the owner as compliance officer, which lowers the pressure to buy. One positive: ECIJA describes bill 18.241-03 as requiring broker registration, AML policies, beneficial-owner checks, cash-transaction reporting and 10-year record keeping, with a 24-month adaptation period. Its legislative stage is unverified.
